analysis: MARKET & PORTFOLIO REVIEW: SPY is in a modest uptrend (+0.4% vs SMA50, slope +1.11%) — not euphoric, but supportive of selective long exposure. The honest self-assessment here is sobering: 8.3% win rate, Profit Factor 0.03x, Sortino -15.40. These are not statistical noise — the strategy has been forcing entries too early and/or in names without true asymmetry. The mandate is clear: protect capital, be highly selective, keep most cash idle. POSITION REVIEW: NVDA (+4.45%) is the only winner and thesis remains intact — AI capex cycle is strong, forward P/E 14.49, PEG 0.48, EPS revisions +22.4%. Hold. MCO (-3.47%) is within normal drawdown; thesis (financial data moat) intact; watch earnings. FOXA (-1.84%) is noise; small loss, hold unless thesis breaks at earnings. AMP (-9.05%) is the most concerning — this is the THIRD time we have entered AMP and been stopped out or badly underwater. Down 9%, already two prior stops hit. The thesis appears structurally challenged for this name. If current price is approaching the original stop level, exit discipline should prevail; at minimum, do NOT add to AMP. CANDIDATE SCREENING: Two names stand out from the 30-candidate list. IT (Gartner) is the single best setup: UPTREND basing at 44% of its 52-week range, forward P/E of 11.36 (extremely cheap for a high-quality compounder), PEG 0.74, ROE 113.6%, and EPS revisions +6.9% upward — analysts are upgrading estimates into what appears to be a durable demand inflection. The only concern is slightly negative revenue growth (-0.6%) and earnings in 34 days, but the valuation cushion is substantial. CRM (Salesforce) also has merit — strong FCF ($17.7B), forward P/E 14.08, PEG 0.76, UPTREND extending with +18% SMA50 slope — but at 66% of its 52-week range and already extended, it's not in the ideal basing entry window. Given the portfolio's poor track record and the directive to protect capital, I recommend ONE new position (IT) sized conservatively, keeping ~48% of equity in cash as a deliberate choice rather than a failure.

trades.entry_strategy: Limit order at $185.85 or better; will also accept entry on a 1-3% pullback toward $180-183 which would improve risk/reward. Do not chase above $192. Earnings on Nov 3 (34 days) — size is already conservative enough to hold through earnings unless price breaks stop first.
trades.rationale: FUNDAMENTAL: Gartner is an exceptional quality compounder — ROE 113.6%, operating margin 22.6%, FCF $1.1B, and fortress-like pricing power via subscription research contracts with near-100% renewal rates. The critical insight is the valuation: forward P/E of 11.36 with PEG 0.74 is deeply anomalous for a business of this quality. Analysts have raised EPS estimates +6.9% in the last 60 days suggesting an earnings inflection is in progress even as revenue growth is temporarily flat (-0.6% — likely mix shift, not demand erosion). Historically Gartner trades at 18-22x forward earnings; mean-reversion to 16x forward alone implies 40%+ upside. TECHNICAL: Price is in a confirmed UPTREND (basing) at 44% of its 52-week range — this is the preferred Stage 1-to-2 transition window. SMA50 slope is +12.6% (healthy acceleration), price is +3.8% above SMA50 (not extended), and it has recovered meaningfully from the $125.73 low without becoming overextended. ATR(14) is 4.3%, so a 1.92x ATR stop at $170.50 places the loss-control level below the recent basing structure.
trades.exit_plan: STOP: Hard stop at $170.50. THESIS BREAK: Exit if Gartner reports declining subscription renewal rates or meaningful EPS miss at Nov 3 earnings. TIME STOP: If price is flat or lower 90 days from entry with no fundamental progress, reassess and free capital. TARGET: Trim 50% at $222 (~19% gain), let remainder run toward $240-250 if momentum persists. LTCG consideration: If entry gains hold past 12 months and thesis intact, consider holding for tax efficiency — but capital protection takes priority over tax optimization.
